priorAbsorption: MAO-OA-T3 added the bounded local launcher. BRIGADE-MAO-R1 enriched that same owner with an injected atomic delegation lifecycle coordinator for parent/global reservation, abort cascade, exactly-once release and serialized completion, then added a file-backed durable delegation ledger store (reserve/settle/abortCascade append-only replay, mirroring MaoFileRunStore) so coordinator state survives crash/restart without double-release or double-wake. BRIGADE-MAO-R1-R2 hardened launch()'s discarded-settlement-failure defect and requestCancellation's silent-abort-failure defect, and added a per-acquisition lockfile ownership token. BRIGADE-MAO-R1-R3 found the R2 token check was still non-atomic (a read-then-unlink pair of syscalls) and removed automatic stale-lock takeover entirely, failing closed instead; it also extended the recovery path to cover the adapter-rejection and post-reservation run-store-failure windows using a caller-supplied launchIdempotencyKey. BRIGADE-MAO-R1-R4 (reviewer RETURN_FOR_REWORK) found the R3 recovery path still trusted an unverified caller-supplied identity (absence of durable evidence for ANY key, including a wrong one, was treated as authorization to settle) and found the R3 admin lock-recovery function was still exported from the runtime/public barrel, reachable while writers could still be active. Fixes: reservations now durably bind launchIdempotencyKey/childTaskId/reservationKey together at the reservation boundary (ledger schema v3); settle/settleDurable accept an optional expectedIdentity verified against the reservation's own persisted identity BEFORE any settlement, returning IDENTITY_MISMATCH (no state change, capacity remains reserved) on a wrong/stale/unrelated caller identity; reconcileDelegation routes every attempt-scoped recovery through this verification. The R3 admin lock-recovery function is renamed, requires a literal true acknowledgment argument with no default, and is deliberately not re-exported from the runtime barrel at all - reachable only via a direct file-scoped import for offline maintenance tooling, guarded by source-boundary tests asserting the barrel's own text never names it. BRIGADE-MAO-R1-R5 (reviewer RETURN_FOR_REWORK) found two further gaps: (1) MaoDurableDelegationPort.settleDurable still accepted an OPTIONAL identity, so a runtime consumer could omit it entirely and settle unverified; (2) reconcileDelegation's TERMINAL-STATE recovery path (distinct from the R4 attempt-scoped path) settled using a caller-supplied reservationKey with no verification that it actually belonged to the terminal task being recovered, so a terminal task A's outcome could durably settle an unrelated task B's still-open reservation. Fixes: settleDurable's expectedIdentity parameter is now REQUIRED at the type level, with a runtime MISSING_IDENTITY guard for any caller that bypasses the type system; a new read-only getReservationIdentity port method resolves a reservation's own durably bound identity without settling it; reconcileDelegation's terminal-state path now resolves the reservation's own identity, verifies childTaskId matches the requested taskId, and uses only the reservation's own durable identity to settle, returning identityMismatch (no state change) otherwise; inline launcher settlement (launch()'s own success/adapter-rejected paths) now sources identity from its own already-durable reservation receipt rather than reconstructing it. Per explicit operator instruction, the R3/R4 offline force-unlock helper (and its result type) was REMOVED FROM THE SOURCE MODULE ENTIRELY, not merely left unexported from the barrel; automatic stale-lock acquisition continues to fail closed with no programmatic recovery path anywhere in the package, and the module documents a manual, out-of-band, operator-performed lockfile deletion as the only recovery procedure. New adversarial tests prove a durably-succeeded Task A cannot settle a sibling Task B's still-open reservation (fails closed with identityMismatch, reservation B remains open, no new SETTLE entry), and that a type-system-bypassing caller supplying undefined/null/partial identity to settleDurable is rejected with MISSING_IDENTITY while leaving the reservation untouched and re-settleable. Deterministic integration and durable crash/replay through the real launcher are proven by tests (84/84 focused MAO delegation tests, 1973/1973 full Execution Plane suite, all passing across repeated runs); representative operator-authorized runtime pilot remains pending and was not run this round (OPERATOR_RUNTIME_PILOT_AUTHORIZED=NO binding throughout). BRIGADE-MAO-R1-R6 (reviewer RETURN_FOR_REWORK) found two further gaps: (1) MaoFileDelegationLedgerStore.settle - the PUBLIC concrete-store method, distinct from and reachable independently of the narrower MaoDurableDelegationPort.settleDurable - still accepted an OPTIONAL expectedIdentity, so any holder of a store instance could settle unverified even though the port boundary alone had been hardened in R5; the underlying coordinator's own public settle had the identical gap, and a type-bypassing caller could still settle with no runtime guard at all at that layer. (2) reconcileDelegation's terminal-state recovery path verified only childTaskId against the reservation's bound identity, which is insufficient to distinguish a genuinely DIFFERENT launch attempt for the SAME taskId - a reservation OLD (task-a/launch-old) left open could be settled by terminal evidence that actually belongs to a LATER, different attempt NEW (task-a/launch-new), because childTaskId alone cannot tell the two attempts apart and the terminal path never inspected which attempt actually produced the terminal event. Fixes: MaoAtomicDelegationLifecycleCoordinator.settle now REQUIRES expectedIdentity at both the type level and via a runtime guard (rejecting undefined/null/malformed identities with IDENTITY_MISMATCH), with all internal trusted settlement (abortCascade's own cascade, ledger replay re-applying already-persisted entries) routed through a new PRIVATE settleTrusted/settleInternal path that is not reachable from outside the coordinator class; MaoFileDelegationLedgerStore.settle received the identical required-identity-plus-runtime-guard treatment as settleDurable, so there is no public method anywhere in this package's runtime surface, at any layer, that settles without a verified identity. reconcileDelegation's terminal-state path now resolves the EXACT launch attempt identity that produced the terminal event (via a new launchIdempotencyKeyOfEvent helper that reverses the launcher's own deterministic ${launchIdempotencyKey}::${milestone} idempotency-key encoding on the terminal event itself) and requires that resolved attempt identity to match the reservation's own durably bound launchIdempotencyKey in addition to childTaskId before ever settling; a terminal event whose producing attempt cannot be resolved, or does not match, fails closed with identityMismatch and no settlement - it never falls back to taskId-only aggregate state. New adversarial tests prove: a same-task, cross-attempt scenario (reservation OLD under launch-old, a separate later attempt NEW under launch-new reaching a durable terminal state for the same taskId) cannot have OLD consumed by NEW's outcome (fails closed with identityMismatch, OLD remains open, no new SETTLE entry, confirmed as a genuine regression guard by verifying the test fails when the fix is disabled); the concrete store's own public settle (not just settleDurable) rejects a missing identity and wrong key/task/reservation identities exactly like the port method; the coordinator's own public settle rejects a bypassed-type-system missing/null identity and a wrong identity, while abortCascade's internal trusted settlement continues to work unaffected through the private path. All 88 focused MAO delegation tests (up from 84) and 1977 full Execution Plane tests (up from 1973) pass, confirmed stable across three consecutive repeated runs; representative operator-authorized runtime pilot remains pending and was not run this round (OPERATOR_RUNTIME_PILOT_AUTHORIZED=NO binding throughout). BRIGADE-MAO-R1 FINAL STABILIZATION PACKET (reviewer RETURN_FOR_REWORK, scope frozen to this one defect) found that R6's OWN fix for the cross-attempt gap was itself unsound: `launchIdempotencyKeyOfEvent` recovered a durable event's producing launch attempt by splitting its `idempotencyKey` string at the FIRST `"::"` - lossy, and directly exploitable, because a real `launchIdempotencyKey` that itself contains `"::"` (e.g. `"launch-old::different-attempt"`) would be misread as merely its own prefix up to that first `"::"`, producing a FALSE match against an unrelated, genuinely shorter reservation identity. Fix: `launchIdempotencyKeyOfEvent` was deleted entirely - there is no reverse-parsing of idempotency keys anywhere in this module any more. A new `terminalEventOwnedByAttempt` function proves (never infers) whether a task's current durably terminal event was produced by a SPECIFIC candidate `launchIdempotencyKey`, using FULL, EXACT string comparison only, keyed to the terminal event's own `eventType`: `INVOCATION_COMPLETED` is compared directly against `milestoneIdempotencyKey(candidateKey, "INVOCATION_COMPLETED")`; `TIMEOUT_DETECTED`/`CANCEL_ACCEPTED` (neither of which is itself keyed by the invocation attempt) are proven instead through the latest preceding `INVOCATION_STARTED` event for the same task, located by durable `.sequence` (never array position) and compared against `milestoneIdempotencyKey(candidateKey, "INVOCATION_STARTED")`; any other terminal event shape, or any inability to locate a required preceding event, fails closed. `latestEventFor` was also corrected to select by `.sequence` explicitly rather than relying on an unstated array-order assumption. New adversarial tests prove, and were confirmed (by deliberately reintroducing the lossy-parsing logic and re-running) to be genuine regression guards, not vacuous assertions: (a) a launchIdempotencyKey of "launch-old::different-attempt" cannot spoof a reservation genuinely bound to the shorter "launch-old"; (b) a legitimate key that itself contains "::" still recovers its own reservation correctly, both through a genuine fault-injected dangling-reservation recovery and an idempotent-replay check; (c) a durably timed-out attempt settles only its own reservation, never a different reservation for the same taskId, proven via the INVOCATION_STARTED-based ownership check; (d) a durably cancelled attempt settles only its own reservation via the identical check. All prior R1-R6 same-task OLD/NEW and cross-task A/B adversarial guards remain passing unchanged. 92/92 focused MAO delegation tests (up from 88) and 1981/1981 full Execution Plane tests (up from 1977) pass, confirmed stable across three consecutive repeated runs; representative operator-authorized runtime pilot remains pending and was not run this round (OPERATOR_RUNTIME_PILOT_AUTHORIZED=NO binding throughout). Scope was held frozen to this one attempt-evidence correlation defect - no locking, reservation-semantics, or architecture changes were made.
